issue_context.title: BUG:dataframe.groupby('some_column').timedelta.sum() results wrong when timedelta contains NaT (pandas=1.3.0)
issue_context.body:
- [y] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [y] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [ ] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

**Note**: Please read [this guide](https://matthewrocklin.com/blog/work/2018/02/28/minimal-bug-reports) detailing how to provide the necessary information for us to reproduce your bug.

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example
this is a tiny example
```python
tmp = pd.DataFrame({'id': ['1624477460271-3908654213', '1624477460271-3908654213'], 'dt':[np.nan, pd.to_timedelta('0:0:2')]})
tmp
Out[6]: 
                         id              dt
0  1624477460271-3908654213             NaT
1  1624477460271-3908654213 0 days 00:00:02
```
#### Problem description

dataframe.groupby('some_column').timedelta.sum() results wrong when timedelta contains NaT
```python
tmp.groupby('id').dt.sum()
Out[7]: 
id
1624477460271-3908654213   -106752 days +00:12:45.145224192
Name: dt, dtype: timedelta64[ns]
```

#### Expected Output
```python
tmp.dt.sum()
Out[8]: Timedelta('0 days 00:00:02')
```
#### Output of ``pd.show_versions()``

<details>

[pandas 1.3.0]

</details>

@phofl  Here is a full copy-pastable example :

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    'a': [1, 1, 2, 2],
    'b': [pd.Timedelta('1d'), pd.Timedelta('2d'), pd.Timedelta('3d'), pd.NaT],
})

print('\ndf:')
print(df)

print('\ndf.dtypes:')
print(df.dtypes)

print('\ndf.groupby(\'a\').b.sum():')
print(df.groupby('a').b.sum())
```

review_comments: can we share code with L523 (ok if its a followon)
not ATM, L523 funcs have mask args that this doesnt (for now at least)

in #43467, `mask` and `result_mask` parameters were added to `_libs.groupby.group_mean` so that the same call could be made to `mean` as ` min` and `max`. For consistency, should either remove those unused parameters from `_libs.groupby.group_mean` or add the unused parameters to `_libs.groupby.group_add` also.
